The committed model graph owns node identity and dependencies. Keep the original
IDs and questions. Public execution records must distinguish ready, blocked,
running, native-settled, recorded, assessed, invalidated and closed work.
Native completion is separate from model acceptance. Use returned action IDs;
late sibling results do not change the action that owns a tool or a file.

Record useful results and limitations at substantive boundaries. Do not create
a step for each tool or response. Do not repeat long child answers as progress.
Readers can open the result details and follow exact immutable references.
Report graph revisions and recomputation reasons. A result version remains
available after supersession; a new computation never silently rewrites it.

Planning, source access, native execution, model responses and dependency or
capacity waits have different meanings. Claim overlap only from actual child
start/end observations. A ready list or configured worker count is not proof.

Show the actual declared node, exact consumed result version, saved proposal and parent judgment. Raw-source permission is not proof of reuse. Distinguish confirmed rejection from unknown persistence and final delivery from saved bytes.

Follow the shared absolute work window. Prefer a useful bounded draft; reserve parent integration and finish time. Limited inputs require exact assessed result acceptance; never silently release a future limited input.
